gloss: salted dried fish; salt-preserved dried seafood

definitions.gloss: salted dried fish; salt-preserved dried seafood
definitions.explanation: Seafood that has been preserved by salting and then drying. A traditional Japanese food preservation method that produces ingredients with concentrated flavor, commonly used in everyday cooking.

examples.japanese: {塩干物|しおひもの}を{焼|や}いて{食|た}べる。
examples.english: I grill salted dried fish and eat it.

examples.japanese: この{店|みせ}は{塩干物|しおひもの}の{品揃|しなぞろ}えが{豊富|ほうふ}だ。
examples.english: This shop has a wide selection of salted dried seafood.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}の{沿岸部|えんがんぶ}では、{昔|むかし}から{塩干物|しおひもの}が{保存食|ほぞんしょく}として{重宝|ちょうほう}されてきた。
examples.english: In Japan's coastal areas, salted dried seafood has long been valued as a preserved food.

notes:
Composed of {塩|しお} (salt), {干|ひ} (dried), and {物|もの} (thing). A category of preserved seafood products that includes items like {干物|ひもの} (dried fish) that have been additionally salted. Common examples include salted and dried horse mackerel, sardines, and squid.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {塩干物|しおひもの}を{焼|や}く: to grill salted dried fish
- {塩干物|しおひもの}{売|う}り{場|ば}: salted dried fish section (in a store)
- {塩干物|しおひもの}の{加工|かこう}: processing of salted dried seafood

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {干物|ひもの}: dried fish — may or may not be salted; the broader category
- {塩鮭|しおざけ}: salted salmon — a specific type of salted fish
- {燻製|くんせい}: smoked food — preserved by smoking rather than salt-drying
